decision.go: Finite analytic reference for one supported conditional correction and normalized evidence.
decision.no_go: Standalone remedy for historical SOC/Q undercoverage, drop-in conversion of the archived impossible moment pair, or streaming estimator adoption without prediction/full-box closure.

representation.variables: x in R^16; q=x[5]=log(Q_Ah), z=x[11], h=x[15]. C={a<=h<=b}, normally a=-1,b=1.
representation.persistent_semantics: m,K are Gaussian KERNEL parameters, not the physical supported mean/covariance. Retain the kernel and the support descriptor; physical moments are derived. A kernel center may lie outside C.
representation.non_gaussian_joint: For K_hh>0, let d=K[:,h]/K_hh and C_res=K-K[:,h]K[h,:]/K_hh. Draw H from the scalar truncated normal and independent eta~N(0,C_res); X=m+d(H-m_h)+eta. This keeps every SOC/logQ correlation and the non-Gaussian joint shape.
representation.migration: The saved physical moment pair mean_h=1 with positive variance has no supported-distribution inverse. Reinterpreting that pair as a kernel changes the belief and is not an exact warm migration.

scalar_moments.variance: v_T=s^2*[1+(alpha*phi(alpha)-beta*phi(beta))/Z-lambda^2]. Infinite-endpoint terms t*phi(t) have limit zero.
scalar_moments.positive_variance: With positive kernel variance and a nonempty finite interval, a<m_T<b and v_T>0. Contact of the kernel center with a bound does not imply a deterministic physical state.
scalar_moments.contraction_proof: For normalized truncated scalar density f and mean m_T, integration of d[(h-m_T)f(h)]/dh gives 1-v_T/s^2=(b-m_T)f(b)-(a-m_T)f(a)>=0. Thus 0<=v_T<=s^2 and V<=K in PSD order.

correction_and_evidence.likelihood: y=c+J^T x+epsilon, epsilon~N(0,R), R>0; c,J,R are frozen for this reference likelihood.
correction_and_evidence.reason: Gaussian product identity: N(x;m,K)*Normal(y;c+J^T x,R)=Normal(y;c+J^T m,S)*N(x;m_plus,K_plus). Integrate over C and divide by the prior support normalizer.
correction_and_evidence.exactly_once: The support indicator is part of the prior, not another observation. The normalizer ratio telescopes over distinct measurements. Source/sample cursor ownership must separately prevent reusing an observation.
correction_and_evidence.two_observation_identity: For two distinct independent-noise observations, evidence1*evidence2 = unconstrained Gaussian joint predictive density(y1,y2)*Z_2/Z_0. Sequential and batch kernel parameters and final supported moments agree.
correction_and_evidence.no_voltage_cutoff: Every finite y is evaluated under the declared Gaussian likelihood. There is no voltage residual acceptance threshold, truth-based scale or added covariance multiplier. Numerical loss of evaluability is reported as numerical failure, not as evidence rejection.
correction_and_evidence.linearization_location: If this reference is later embedded in a nonlinear model, form an affine likelihood at an admissible physical location, not automatically at the possibly out-of-domain kernel center. That future approximation is outside this exact reference.

zero_information.condition: J=0, or more generally K J=0. Then the likelihood is constant on the Gaussian support.
zero_information.identity: m_plus=m, K_plus=K, Z_plus=Z_prior, M_plus=M, V_plus=V; evidence is the constant likelihood density. Missing voltage instead contributes evidence factor1.
zero_information.negative_control: Converting the supported M,V into a new Gaussian kernel and truncating it again changes the distribution even when J=0. Example: N(0,1) restricted to h<=0 has M=-sqrt(2/pi), V=1-2/pi. Reinterpreting M,V as a Gaussian and restricting again decreases M and V again. This violates zero-information invariance.
zero_information.weight_note: A constant within-component likelihood may still distinguish different components if their constants differ. With the same c,R across components and J=0, weights also remain unchanged.

singular_case.PSD_requirement: K_hh=0 in a PSD matrix implies K[:,h]=0. A nonzero cross row with zero diagonal is invalid, not a branch to regularize.
singular_case.inside: If a<=m_h<=b, h=m_h almost surely, Z=1, M=m,V=K. Use ordinary Gaussian conditioning on remaining directions; no division by K_hh. The boundary value h=1 is allowed when its variance was genuinely zero.
singular_case.outside: If m_h is outside [a,b], Z=0 and there is no supported prior or posterior. Report an invalid zero-mass prior before evaluating voltage. Do not clip, reseed or fabricate variance.
singular_case.tiny_positive: A positive variance remains positive; no arbitrary small-variance threshold changes it into the singular branch.

SOC_Q_reporting.linear_marginal: For T=t^T X, write T=m_t+d_t(H-m_h)+eta_t, d_t=K_th/K_hh and Var(eta_t)=K_tt-K_th^2/K_hh. Its CDF is the one-dimensional integral over h in[a,b] of phi((h-m_h)/s)/s * Phi((t_value-m_t-d_t(h-m_h))/sqrt(Var(eta_t))), divided by Z. For zero residual variance use the deterministic indicator limit.
SOC_Q_reporting.SOC: Use the supported z marginal and declared quantile probability; mean +/-2 SD is not its exact nominal-probability interval.
SOC_Q_reporting.capacity: Q=exp(q), so F_Q(Q)=F_q(log(Q)) and Q quantiles are exp(q quantiles). exp(E[q]) is not E[Q].
SOC_Q_reporting.capacity_raw_moments: For k=1,2, E[Q^k]=exp(k*m_q+0.5*k^2*K_qq)*Z(m_h+k*K_hq,K_hh)/Z(m_h,K_hh). Here Z uses the same h bounds. Var(Q)=E[Q^2]-E[Q]^2.
SOC_Q_reporting.claim_limit: Nominal posterior probability is conditional on the specified reference distribution. It does not establish calibrated frequentist coverage or historical adequacy.

undercoverage_counterexample.rank_one_limitation: After the voltage update, support changes chart covariance only by a negative-semidefinite rank-one term along K_plus[:,h], and moves the mean only along that direction.
undercoverage_counterexample.decisive_case: If K_plus[z,h]=K_plus[q,h]=0, conditioning on h leaves the complete joint z,q marginal unchanged. An already biased, too-narrow SOC/logQ marginal therefore remains biased and too narrow. This disproves a general interval-repair claim for the support operation.
undercoverage_counterexample.historical_loss: This operation does not recover an old nonlinear likelihood, change unrepresented parameter alternatives, or establish when prior covariance became inadequate.
undercoverage_counterexample.covariance_growth_distinction: The supported posterior can have larger variance than the PREVIOUS supported prior when an observation moves mass away from a boundary. Contraction is relative to its own updated Gaussian kernel, not a claim of physical-marginal monotonicity over observations.
undercoverage_counterexample.growth_example: Scalar h in[-1,1], prior kernel N(1,1), observation y=-1 under y=h+epsilon and R=1. Updated kernel is N(0,1/2). Prior variance is 1-2*phi(2)/[Phi(0)-Phi(-2)]-[(phi(2)-phi(0))/[Phi(0)-Phi(-2)]]^2; posterior variance is 0.5*[1-2*sqrt(2)*phi(sqrt(2))/(2*Phi(sqrt(2))-1)]. The latter is larger (approximately0.2537 versus0.2513). This is a scalar analytic illustration, not a run.

closure_limits.full_box: A single h restriction does not constrain any other Gaussian coordinate to its physical range. A full-box truncated Gaussian also closes under an affine Gaussian likelihood, but needs its multivariate support normalizer and actual joint moments; the scalar formula does not supply them.
closure_limits.affine_prediction: For an invertible affine map, the Gaussian kernel transforms affinely but its truncation slab also transforms. An axis-aligned h slab stays axis aligned only under special maps. Even h_next=A*h+B with fixed A>0 requires carrying the transformed interval[A*a+B,A*b+B]; replacing it with the larger physical[-1,1] interval changes the law.
closure_limits.nonlinear_prediction: The real transition depends nonlinearly on Q,tau and gamma. The supported Gaussian family is not closed under that pushforward. Real voltage also includes nonlinear OCV and H*h. A re-projection after prediction or nonlinear conditioning is an additional approximation requiring its own contract; repeated moment re-truncation is not exact closure.
closure_limits.storage: A scalar-support kernel can use16 kernel means plus136 factor entries, with a support descriptor and optional log-normalizer cache. Derived physical moments, numerical normalizer workspace and any prediction-closure state must be budgeted separately. This is not a complete10KiB implementation claim.

finite_qualification_proposal.scope: Only fabricated affine reference calculations; no canonical states, nonlinear model calls or learner runs.
finite_qualification_proposal.common: 16D with q index5,z index11,h index15; h bounds[-1,1]. Other13 axes may be fixed independent N(0,0.01) because they factor out of this reference likelihood; this deliberately claims only h support.
finite_qualification_proposal.interior: h~N(0,0.04), z~N(0.5,0.0004), q~N(log(0.06),0.0009), independent. c=2.97,J_z=1.5,J_h=0, all other J=0,R=0.0001,y=3.8. The support normalizer ratio is1; ordinary Gaussian z correction, unchanged q and unchanged supported h law.
finite_qualification_proposal.outward: H~N(1,0.04), z=0.5+0.1*(H-1)+eps_z with Var(eps_z)=0.0004, q=log(0.06)-0.3*(H-1)+eps_q with Var(eps_q)=0.0009. Independent residuals. c=2.97,J_z=1.5,J_h=-0.02,R=0.0001,y=3.8. S=0.001676,r=0.1,m_h_plus=1+0.00052/0.001676>1. Require actual mean_h<1, positive variance and the full correlated supported formulas.
finite_qualification_proposal.zero_information: Reuse the outward case posterior KERNEL and support, set J=0 and choose any frozen finite c,y with R=0.0001. Require exact kernel identity, unchanged physical law, correct constant evidence; show moment-retruncate negative control changes the law.
finite_qualification_proposal.branch_checks: Exactly zero h variance with h=1 and zero cross row is valid; h=1.01 is zero-mass invalid. Two distinct outward-family observations, e.g.y1=3.8,y2=3.72 with unchanged c,J,R, must match joint Gaussian evidence times Z2/Z0 and batch final kernel. Include the scalar covariance-growth example as an algebraic branch assertion.
finite_qualification_proposal.numerics: Use log support probabilities and stable tail ratios; positive interval mass may underflow in ordinary probability space. Numerical tolerances qualify reconstruction accuracy only and are never voltage-error acceptance thresholds.
finite_qualification_proposal.finish_line: One finite qualification receipt and reviewed GO for reference correctness / NO-GO for standalone SOC/Q remedy or streaming adoption. No automatic canonical experiment.
